title: Conditional moment contraction
statement: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses, let $J$ be a set of coordinates, let $f$ be a real-valued function on the product space, and let $q\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $1\le q$. Then the product expectation of the $q$th power of the absolute value of the conditional expectation over coordinates outside $J$ is at most the product expectation of $|f|^q$.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a finite product probability space with positive coordinate weights summing to one
$f$ is real-valued on the product space
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $J\subseteq[n]$, $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, and $q\ge1$. Then $\mathbb E_P|E_Jf|^q\le\mathbb E_P|f|^q$.
